facts.raw_span: persistent swelling of his left breast for four years
ultrasonography had shown gynecomastia (BIRADS II) attributed to anabolic-steroid use
a new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple
Repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture
Mammography reveals a lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter without microcalcifications (BIRADS III)
anabolic-steroid use, which he discontinued

concepts.why: The patient has a history of persistent swelling of his left breast, which was initially attributed to anabolic-steroid use, a common cause of gynecomastia.
The patient has a new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple, which is consistent with a breast adenoma, a common type of benign breast tumor.
The patient has a solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography, which is consistent with a papilloma, a type of benign breast tumor.
The patient has a lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography, which is consistent with a phyllodes tumor, a rare type of breast tumor.
The patient has a history of anabolic-steroid use, which can cause hormonal imbalances, and may be contributing to his breast symptoms.
The patient has a mildly tender mass under the left nipple, which is consistent with mastitis, a type of breast inflammation.
The patient has a solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography, which is consistent with fat necrosis, a type of breast injury.
The patient has a mildly tender mass under the left nipple, which is consistent with a breast abscess, a type of breast infection.

rationales.F01: Persistent swelling could be related to hormonal imbalance or gynecomastia.
rationales.F02: Previous ultrasonography showing gynecomastia attributed to anabolic-steroid use strongly supports gynecomastia diagnosis.
rationales.F03: A new, mildly tender, firm mass is more suggestive of a tumor or adenoma than gynecomastia.
rationales.F04: Solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography could indicate a tumor or adenoma.
rationales.F05: Lobulated retroareolar mass without microcalcifications is more indicative of a benign tumor like adenoma or phyllodes tumor.
